Found it directly in the pinned corpus clone (grep, then read in context).

`SNAPPY_HAVE_NEON_CRC32` has no single unconditional value in the development source — it's a compile-time gate at `snappy/snappy.cc:55-61`:

```c
#if !defined(SNAPPY_HAVE_NEON_CRC32)
#if SNAPPY_HAVE_NEON && defined(__ARM_FEATURE_CRC32)
#define SNAPPY_HAVE_NEON_CRC32 1
#else
#define SNAPPY_HAVE_NEON_CRC32 0
#endif
#endif  // !defined(SNAPPY_HAVE_NEON_CRC32)
```

So it evaluates to `1` only on ARM builds with NEON and `__ARM_FEATURE_CRC32` (CMake probes this via a `__crc32cw` compile test, `CMakeLists.txt:229`); on all other platforms (including x86) it is `0`. The semantic retrieval (`xerj code`) did not surface the `#define` block itself — I confirmed it by grepping the corpus clone at `/root/.xerj-code/corpora/snappy`.

ANSWER: 0 (1 only when SNAPPY_HAVE_NEON && defined(__ARM_FEATURE_CRC32); otherwise 0)
